newsitem.title: NORWAY: New Norway PM pledges economic continuity.
newsitem.headline: New Norway PM pledges economic continuity.

text.p: Norway's new Labour prime minister Thorbjoern Jagland pledged on Tuesday that his government would pursue the economic policies of his predecessor Gro Harlem Brundtland.
He told parliament the minority government's goals remained to achieve full employment and create an ecologically sustainable society in the oil-rich Nordic country.
"The government will carry forward the policy of the Harlem Brundtland government," he said in a formal government declaration.

"It is of special importance to have the economy firmly under control so that the high oil profits the country will enjoy in the next few years do not turn into new price rises destructive to society.
"This is the foundation for a continued fight against unemployment," said Jagland, repeating statements made to reporters last Friday when he took office.
Jagland replaced Brundtland, who has dominated Norwegian politics for 15 years and was in office for 10 of them.
Brundtland stepped down to give heir-apparent Jagland the opportunity to warm up to the task of leading the government into the general election in September next year.

Jagland's first test of strength will be to shepherd the 1997 state budget through a hostile parliament, and he has said that changes to the draft would have to be made in order for it to be accepted.
The government is under pressure from the opposition right and left of centre to use the massive oil wealth to increase expenditure before the budget is adopted in December.
The 1997 budget is projected to show a surplus of 40.9 billion crowns, but the government has said it will keep a tight grip on the money purse for fear of fuelling inflation.
Norway, pumping about three million barrels per day, is the world's second largest oil exporter after Saudi Arabia.
